## 2. Product, authority and workflow

BRIO (`brio_unlocker`) is a local-only visual customization and practice/modifier layer for buildroyale.io. Changes affect the current browser's rendering. Native server state, entitlement/ownership, outgoing start packets, WebSocket traffic and MessagePack remain native. There is no requirement for other players to see BRIO cosmetics. Preserve this scope unless the user explicitly changes it.

Each iteration has two goals: complete features already supported by evidence, and gather missing evidence for the rest. The user explicitly reopened player/chest/airdrop indicators and expanded the surface beyond the earlier five-item V35 priority. The older instruction to finish those five before opening other surfaces is superseded.

Maximize useful passive information in every game: native objects and resource types, captured arrays, container identity/state changes, HUD values, build/deployable/spellfield metadata, source candidates, indicator eligibility/suppression, and bounded player metadata audits. Capture novelty and meaningful changes, not repeated empty baselines or noisy full snapshots. Do not make the user repeatedly press CONTENT BASE/AFTER or BOT WATCH. Those manual recon tasks were retired.

Limit each match to at most **three different additional manual action types**. A type may be repeated. Normal gameplay is not a recon task. The current V41 procedure needs two: MATCH START once and full-map inspection after meteor expiry. COPY RESULTS after the match is export, not another gameplay burden. Add a third type only when it resolves a concrete uncertainty and specify what to do and when.

Never discard a modifier because it is difficult, inconvenient, or one probe failed. A failed route may be retired when exhaustively verified, with the missing required data and evidence documented; unresolved features remain unresolved. Chest/airdrop/fishing contents and bot identification are not scrapped. The user's earlier willingness to justify impossible features does not authorize premature retirement. Static bot detection may be stopped only after exhausting bundle/game-state routes; a future behavioral design requires new user direction and must not be silently invented.

## 4. Cosmetic selection contract

| Category | Modes |
|---|---|
| Body / Head / Pickaxe | Native, Random, bundled item, Invisible, Custom |
| Wrap | Native, Random, bundled item |
| Trail / Glider | Native, Random, bundled item, Invisible |
| Emotes | Four independent slots: Native, Random, bundled item |

Body/head use the skin catalog but distinct rendered resources. No Custom/Invisible emotes or wraps; no Custom trail/glider. Native is a text option; default skin is not a duplicate card. Search all available entries, including special/custom modes, with an ordinary text cursor. Allowed native IDs receive `SYNC`, not OWNED: this does not establish purchase entitlement. Catalog/allowed counts are dynamic. Trophy/OG Champions pickaxe and sunray wrap are useful proven historical test assets.

Custom uploads retain category-scoped IDs `custom1`, `custom2`, etc., in IndexedDB database `brio_unlocker`, store `customAssets`; body 300×300, head 350×350, pickaxe 300×300. Unsupported historical categories may be ignored but never delete stored uploads. Cosmetic selection uses `br_local_visuals`; Extras uses `brio_extras_state`; native `locker2` is separate. Restore native snapshots when reverting.

Use the current Play name with one leading `uL#` stripped before adding `uL#`, respect native nameBox maxLength, and match the captured renderer with known structure/name and truncated-name handling. Never hardcode `unlocker_test_player` or a human name from logs. IDs remain useful internal diagnostics but the player-ID display modifier has been removed entirely.

Known implementation gap: old requirements call for filtering zero-size/fully transparent previews; corrected V41 only removes a card on image `onerror`. Do not describe broader validation as complete without implementing/verifying it.

Indicators: three independent nearest-target off-screen indicators; all three may display together. Player deep red `#a81020`, airdrop orange `#f28b16`, chest yellow `#ffd21c`. Each 144×72 arrow has text wholly inside the shaft; label is `(native distance / 100)m`, rounded to at most one decimal, no type words. Label follows the arrow rotation, with only a 180° flip for left-pointing arrows. Do not arbitrary-angle counterrotate it out of the shaft. Different margins reduce overlap: 90 player,165 chest,240 airdrop. Use active captured arrays, fresh full native affine transform (≤700ms), canvas size/CSS rect conversion, on-screen/stale/no-target suppression. Culled stale players must not be retained as active targets. Document that this is nearest eligible target logic, not a global map-location guarantee.

Health/shield numbers attach to their own native bars, centered in local bar coordinates, fit font to current width/height and clip to interior. Suppress tiny/zero-width bars. No player-ID option remains. Verify live geometry and readability; mocked clipping alone is not proof.

Recon: bounded bot audit covers all own fields (up to400), non-render metadata two levels (up to100 objects, primitive arrays ≤32), delayed settled sample ~2s and changes during45s, capped at60players/two snapshots each; no heuristic labels. 1. Reload Build Royale home; run the entire corrected direct minified V41 from the appendix or `dist/brio-v41.min.js` once restored. Wait for READY; report absent UI/readiness as a failure rather than assuming it ran.
2. Extras → Modifiers: enable all nine blue flags: Player health bars; Nearest player indicator; Nearest chest indicator; Nearest airdrop indicator; Permanent meteor location; Health/shield numbers; Low-health visual warning; Low-material warning; Identify bots. No challenge is required for this focused V41 test. Leave conflicting hide-player/bar challenges off so arrows and bars can be assessed; do not reset unrelated saved settings silently. Verify the Play settings snapshot in the log.
3. Start a match; press MATCH START once when gameplay begins. Play normally. Observe numbers contained in health/shield bars and the three independent arrow types, their colors/meters/contained labels, on-screen disappearance and ordinary performance. If low health/materials occurs naturally, note the warning behavior; do not add resource-draining manual chores.
4. After a meteor marker appears and its usual native expiry passes, open the full map to verify it is still visible. No meteor arm action. Record absence of a meteor spawn as 'not exercised', not a feature failure. If convenient observe native map/minimap behavior, without claiming either surface passed unless actually seen.
5. After the match, COPY RESULTS. Include complete output without trimming source/audit entries, plus visual observations: version readiness, selected settings, phase-button use, meteor appearance/expiry/retention, arrow containment/color/meters, numbers, warnings, performance, errors. Paste/upload as `logs/v41-2026-10-05-match-01.txt` (increment match number for additional runs). On GitHub, Add file → Create new file at that path, or Upload files. Preserve raw data; observations may precede it clearly labeled.

Only two additional action types during play. Optional future tests must state at most three action types, when to perform them, exact selections and expected evidence. A meteor absent from a match, no nearby container, or no naturally low health is an unexercised condition; do not fabricate coverage.

## 9. Engineering and validation contract

Prefer native renderer/container attachment and cached resources. Initial global `Array.prototype.push/unshift` capture is temporary (maximum12s), restoring when local renderer and required roofs are found or at timeout. Thereafter use own methods on captured native arrays. No persistent broad Canvas hooks, requestAnimationFrame wrappers, global mutation observers or high-frequency whole-world scans. The exception for emotes is an exact four native icon-path src setter with bounded720000ms restoration; keep it narrow and clean up. Avoid treating recon-only interception as final architecture.

V41 timing: native feature attachment/cleanup ~2s; passive recon12s; player indicator250ms; chest/airdrop500ms; bot sampling500ms with bounded metadata45s; meteor fallback scan1000ms capped3000 nodes; terminal text flush200ms. Source probing is passive same-origin fetch/inspection, not execution of discovered strings. Protect against getter/proxy/circular metadata, unavailable nodes, unloaded images, stale arrays/transforms, native descriptor restrictions and object destruction. Never read every render graph continuously to satisfy 'maximum recon'.

Cleanup/rearm restores original hooks and descriptors, array methods, resources/opacity/parent remove/destruction, src/emote adapters, temporary interceptors and native UI; removes tracking/inventory/feature nodes, overlays and timers. Preserve selected/custom data. Existing tests are smoke/mocks, not a live browser proof. Both corrected source and minified output passed Node syntax checks and integrated mock boot/Play/settings/copy/cleanup/reinjection, all-three arrows/colors/meters, on-screen/stale/culling suppression, automatic meteor acquisition through a native-like prototype `add`, native retention/restoration, numeric centering/interior clipping and zero-width suppression, warnings and bounded audits. `errors:[]` is scoped to those mocked runs. Never promise absence of every runtime error.

Minification used Babel with scope-aware identifier mangling, preserving property keys/native Unicode field names. The previous local helper depended on a temporary Babel bundle; reproduce with a standard available toolchain and verify output rather than assuming that path exists in the new thread. No runtime dependency is needed by the supplied final plain payload. Do not deliver test-only exported builds (`brio_v41.test.min.js`) or the obsolete compressed copy.

## Historical original project knowledge (unabridged)

Frozen historical evidence. It does not override the current sections above.

````````markdown
# BRIO / Build Royale Local-Only Customization — Project Knowledge

## Current snapshot — 2026-09-25

This section is the **current source of truth**. The historical handoff retained later in this file documents how the project reached this point, but any older "next work", "not yet implemented", or server/protocol-oriented direction is superseded by this current snapshot when the two conflict.

The script/project name is:

```text
brio_unlocker
```

The controlled test-player display name is:

```text
unlocker_test_player
```

---

## 1. Settled product goal

BRIO is a **local-only client visual customization layer for buildroyale.io**.

The user's current browser should display BRIO's selections for the local player. There is no requirement for remote clients to see them and no requirement for the match server to recognize the local selections.

The product should therefore modify the local renderer rather than the multiplayer authority path.

Current architecture:

```text
Build Royale home UI
        ↓
BRIO local selection state
        ↓
Play
        ↓
brief local-renderer discovery
        ↓
capture the renderer belonging to unlocker_test_player
        ↓
restore discovery hook immediately
        ↓
replace fields/resources only on that local renderer
        ↓
native game renderer continues normally
```

Do not return to trying to make arbitrary cosmetics server-authoritative.

Specifically, final BRIO should not be designed around:

- rewriting the outbound start packet;
- modifying WebSocket sends;
- modifying `msgpack.encode`;
- persisting fake cosmetics into `locker2`;
- ownership/entitlement spoofing;
- persuading remote clients to render BRIO choices.

`locker2` remains useful as architecture reference and as the game's native state, but BRIO's visual state is separate.

---

## 2. Performance requirement

The user considers meaningful game slowdown unacceptable.

Production rules:

- no persistent per-frame `drawImage` interception;
- no `requestAnimationFrame` wrapper;
- no broad persistent `Array.prototype.push` hook;
- no broad persistent `HTMLImageElement.src` hook;
- no whole-page mutation observer running throughout a match;
- no high-frequency world polling;
- no renderer-independent parallel drawing system unless there is no native-renderer alternative;
- temporary hooks must restore as soon as their narrow purpose is complete.

V14 through V17 established that direct local-renderer substitution can run with normal gameplay performance.

A major regression occurred when V11/V15 tried unresolved custom Trail/Wrap/Glider/Emote mechanisms. That is why final custom support is deliberately narrower.

---

## 3. Current cosmetic support matrix

| Category | Native | Random | Bundled catalog | Invisible | Custom upload |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Body | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Head | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Pickaxe | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Wrap | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| Trail | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Glider | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Emote slot 1 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| Emote slot 2 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| Emote slot 3 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| Emote slot 4 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |

This is an intentional product decision, not merely an unfinished feature list.

Custom support for Wrap/Trail/Glider/Emote was tested and found too touchy/unreliable, including severe performance degradation in custom-heavy matches. Those categories should remain bundled/Native/Random only unless a future completely clean mechanism is discovered.

Invisible Trail and Invisible Glider were later solved cleanly and are supported.

The user's standard pickaxe for test loadouts is:

```text
OG Champions Pickaxe
catalog ID: trophy
```

Use that pickaxe in future cosmetic regression tests unless the test specifically concerns another pickaxe.

---

## 4. Current UI behavior

The custom home UI is intentionally rough/black during engineering, but these interaction requirements are already settled.

### Native button takeover

Use the existing native elements:

```text
#loggedInLocker
#loggedInShop
```

Do not replace those DOM nodes.

BRIO renames them:

```text
Locker → (un)Locker
Shop   → Extras
```

The buttons use capture-phase click interception so the native Locker/Shop panels do not open.

Known working button layout:

```text
178×53
blue Shop-like native styling
Locker margin-right: 0
Extras margin-right: 80px
margin-top: 7px
transition: none
pointer/hand cursor
```

Native IMG children are hidden because the site uses CSS `content:url(...)` hover swapping. BRIO uses its own non-swapped icon span.

### Locker categories

```text
Skins
  Body
  Head
Pickaxes
Wraps
Trails
Gliders
Emotes
  Slot 1
  Slot 2
  Slot 3
  Slot 4
```

Body and Head are independent local-render choices even though Build Royale's native protocol has only one skin ID.

### Special entries

`Native` means:

> leave the game's native renderer selection unchanged for this category.

It is not a "Default" cosmetic and has no preview image.

`Random` resolves to a catalog item for that match.

`Invisible` is shown only in categories where it is supported.

The label must be:

```text
Invisible
```

not "Transparent".

### Search

The search box must use the text/I-beam cursor.

Search filtering applies to **all entries**, including:

```text
Native
Random
Invisible
custom1/custom2/...
catalog cosmetics
```

Do not leave the special entries visible when they do not match the query.

### Broken asset filtering

Catalog preview entries are dynamically removed when:

- the preview fails to load;
- natural dimensions are zero;
- the loaded image is effectively fully transparent/empty.

Examples discovered during recon include `emote50` and earlier `trumperpick`.

Do not rely on a permanent hardcoded blacklist; dynamic validation is preferred.

### Custom uploads

Supported only for:

```text
Body
Head
Pickaxe
```

Uploads:

- persist through page refreshes;
- are isolated per category;
- accumulate instead of replacing the previous custom;
- are named `custom1`, `custom2`, etc.;
- are stored in IndexedDB database `brio_unlocker`, object store `customAssets`;
- are resized to category dimensions.

Current target sizes:

```text
Body     300×300
Head     350×350
Pickaxe  300×300
```

Existing old unsupported custom Wrap/Trail/Glider/Emote records may remain in IndexedDB, but current UI/runtime should hide/ignore them rather than deleting user data.

### No in-match cosmetic menu

Users are not intended to open BRIO's Locker during a match.

V14 temporarily proved that live renderer swapping worked, but that was a diagnostic capability, not a product requirement.

Future modifiers may alter render state during a match automatically, but there should be no user-facing in-match Locker.

---

## 5. Persistence

BRIO visual state is separate from native `locker2`.

Current storage key:

```text
localStorage["br_local_visuals"]
```

Current state shape is approximately:

```javascript
{
  enabled: true,

  body:    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item"|"custom"|"invisible", ...},
  head:    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item"|"custom"|"invisible", ...},
  pickaxe: {mode:"native"|"random"|"item"|"custom"|"invisible", ...},

  wrap:    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item", ...},
  trail:   {mode:"native"|"random"|"item"|"invisible", ...},
  glider:  {mode:"native"|"random"|"item"|"invisible", ...},

  emotes: [
    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item", ...},
    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item", ...},
    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item", ...},
    {mode:"native"|"random"|"item", ...}
  ]
}
```

Old accidental keys such as:

```text
skin
""
```

should be removed/migrated when loading/saving state.

---

## 6. Catalog and SYNC marker

Full catalog source:

```javascript
window.Åèa
```

Current-build catalog counts observed during this project have varied slightly by deployment, e.g. around:

```text
skins      ~179-181
pickaxes   ~167
wraps       76
trails     ~156
gliders      7
emotes     ~209
```

Use the live catalog rather than hardcoded counts.

The current exposed allowed-ID set is:

```javascript
window.åÆÆ
```

On the fresh test account it consisted largely/entirely of the global baseline set.

The UI marker should be called:

```text
SYNC
```

It means the ID is in the game's current allowed/native-valid set; it must not be described as guaranteed account ownership.

Earlier use of `OWNED` was less precise and should not be carried forward.

---

## 7. Direct local-renderer capture — current preferred integration

The stable architecture discovered in V14 is cleaner than the earlier synthetic-ID/decode method.

When Play is clicked:

1. Temporarily replace `Array.prototype.push`.
2. Observe newly inserted objects only until an object matching the local player renderer is created.
3. Identify it by:
   - `renderer["Ée"] === "unlocker_test_player"`;
   - known player-renderer fields such as body/head/container/limb objects.
4. Capture the renderer and the array that contains it.
5. Restore `Array.prototype.push` immediately.
6. Snapshot native renderer resources/values.
7. Apply BRIO selections directly to that one renderer.

This gives per-player isolation and does not modify protocol/network state.

The temporary hook has restored within well under a second in successful tests.

---

## 8. Current renderer cosmetic mapping

Current-build field names are obfuscated and can change. Functional relationships are what matter.

Known working fields:

```text
body sprite resource:
  renderer["Ëå"]["À"]

head sprite resource:
  renderer.head["À"]

head backup/current resource:
  renderer["Äâè"]

pickaxe resource:
  renderer["ÉãÂ"]

currently held item sprite:
  renderer["ä"]["À"]
  (when selected weapon type is "pickaxe")

trail resource prefix:
  renderer["Ëé"]

trail emission timing/state:
  renderer["åëÅ"]

wrap ID:
  renderer["ÆÃÅ"]

glider ID/state:
  renderer["aéÄ"]

glider resource:
  renderer["äÀÊ"]

visible glider sprite resource:
  renderer["ÂÅ"]["À"]

emote effect display:
  renderer["ÄÊâ"]["À"]

left limb primitive:
  renderer["áË"]

right limb primitive:
  renderer["ÄÂ"]

feet primitive:
  renderer["ÄãÀ"]

small player shadow primitive:
  renderer["èÅ"]

player name display:
  renderer["ÃÊ"]

health bar:
  renderer["æÄ"]

shield bar:
  renderer["AÃå"]

player visual/container:
  renderer["Eâ"]
```

Resource objects used successfully by BRIO have the game's expected wrapper shape:

```javascript
{
  src: <url-or-data-url>,
  ÁÄ: <HTMLImageElement>,
  __brio: true,
  ...
}
```

Loaded images are assigned fields such as:

```text
ÀA  = loaded state
ÁÅe = half width
âÅÉ = half height
```

before being inserted into renderer resource wrappers.

---

## 9. Skin and pickaxe behavior

### Bundled Body/Head

Directly assigning independently loaded body/head resource objects to the local renderer works.

This means BRIO can mix:

```text
body from skin A
head from skin B
```

despite the native network/locker model using only one skin ID.

Examples visually proven:

```text
Body: Magma
Head: Devil
```

### Custom Body/Head

Custom Body and Head data-URL resources work through direct renderer assignment.

Earlier source-redirection attempts were unreliable; direct renderer resource assignment is the current path.

### Invisible Body/Head

Transparent body/head image resources alone were not sufficient because the game draws additional local-player primitives.

For full visual invisibility, when Body is Invisible BRIO also sets:

```text
left limb opacity  = 0
right limb opacity = 0
feet opacity       = 0
shadow opacity     = 0
```

This was visually verified.

When the body is not Invisible, restore each primitive to its native captured opacity.

### Pickaxe

Bundled, custom, and Invisible pickaxes work by replacing the local renderer's pickaxe resource.

If the pickaxe is currently held, also update the held-item sprite resource.

Invisible Pickaxe was explicitly reported as visually working after V16.

## 10. Wrap behavior

Bundled wrap substitution is proven.

The player renderer has a wrap identifier:

Setting that to a bundled wrap ID changes the local player's weapon wrap.

`Sun Ray` (`sunray`) is a known successful test value.

The `/cosmetics/combos/<id>.png` path is a locker/catalog preview asset and should not be confused with the actual gun wrap texture pair.

Round 17 proved a much cleaner solution than transparent custom trail images.

## 13. Emote behavior

BRIO supports four independent bundled/Native/Random local emote slots.

Two surfaces must be handled.

### Used emote effect

The local renderer's active emote display object is:

```text
renderer["ÄÊâ"]["À"]
```

A narrow property hook maps the native slot's incoming resource to the selected BRIO bundled emote.

This has visually rendered the selected emotes correctly.

### Emote selection popup/menu

The popup uses the four native slot icon paths:

```text
buildart/emote0.png
buildart/emote1.png
buildart/emote2.png
buildart/emote3.png
```

A narrow `HTMLImageElement.src` setter hook redirects only these exact four paths to the selected bundled emote images.

V17 logged all four menu redirects and no performance regression was reported.

This exact-path hook is the only persistent browser image hook in the current cosmetic architecture.

Custom and Invisible Emotes are intentionally unsupported.

## 14. Performance lessons from V11–V17

### What caused severe slowdown

The bad-performance test injected synthetic IDs for unresolved categories such as:

```text
Wrap
Trail
Glider
Emotes
```

and left a global image setter interception alive waiting for resource paths that did not arrive in the expected way.

A later custom-heavy test similarly used long-lived source substitution for custom extra categories and became very slow.

### What performs normally

These later configurations were reported as normal:

- direct renderer Body/Head/Pickaxe;
- direct bundled Trail/Wrap/Glider;
- direct Invisible Trail;
- direct Invisible Glider;
- narrow bundled emote effect/menu mapping;
- renderer-capture hook restored immediately after spawn.

Therefore future code should stay within those paths unless a new technique is first proven cleanly.

## 21. Test-history ledger from this thread

This ledger is useful because several failed rounds explain why the current design is intentionally narrow.

### V3–V4 — UI/catalog/ownership baseline

Proved native button selectors, responsive shell behavior, catalog access, and the baseline allowed-ID set.

Fresh-account native clickable baseline matched the exposed allowed set.

### V5 — decoded local player substitution

A temporary local `msgpack.decode` wrapper found the local server-created player object and changed only the browser's decoded copy.

Bundled Magma rendered.

This proved local player-specific state substitution but still depended on decode interception.

### V6 — synthetic bundled Body/Head/Pickaxe

Magma Body + Devil Head + Castle Axe rendered.

This proved independent local body/head composition.

Custom logging existed, but later user observation clarified that custom visuals themselves were not actually working correctly yet.

### V7–V8 — server-safe/start-pipeline detour

Attempts to sanitize/commit native server-facing locker state created bugs and did not help the local-only product.

V8 also contained a `ReferenceError: desc is not defined` before its runtime pipeline armed.

This is one reason server-facing manipulation was dropped entirely.

### V9–V10 — heap renderer discovery detour

`queryObjects`/heap approaches were unreliable or unavailable in the execution context.

The renderer was not reached, so default loadouts rendered.

Broken catalog filtering, however, was proven useful and retained.

### V11.2 — local decode + resource redirects

Restored the successful local-only technique.

Bundled Body/Head/Pickaxe worked.
Custom/Invisible Body/Head also began working.

When unresolved synthetic Wrap/Trail/Glider/Emote routes were present, performance became extremely poor.

### V12

Limited runtime substitution back to Body/Head/Pickaxe.

Performance returned to normal.

Mapped extra visible Invisible-body leftovers.

### V13

Targeted probes showed the leftover body pieces were Canvas/render primitives rather than missing image files.

Mapped additional Trail/Glider/Wrap runtime behavior.

### V14 — direct renderer capture

Key architecture breakthrough.

Captured the local renderer directly after Play using a temporary `Array.prototype.push` hook, restored the hook immediately, and assigned local renderer resources/fields directly.

User reported bundled:

```text
skins
pickaxe
wrap
trail
glider
emote effects
```

working.

Emote popup icons were still native.

Invisible body limbs mostly worked but one shadow remained.

### V15

Mapped/fixed the remaining shadow.

Attempted custom support across extra categories.

Custom-extra-category match performance was very bad and custom Trail failed.

Decision: custom runtime support stops at Body/Head/Pickaxe.

### V16

Finalized the intentionally narrower custom scope.

Bundled cosmetics rendered correctly.

Invisible Body/Head had arms/feet/shadow fully suppressed.

User later confirmed Invisible Pickaxe also worked.

Modifier reconnaissance found existing player name/health/shield objects and persistent world renderers.

### V17

Proved:

```text
Invisible Trail
Invisible Glider
```

with normal local-renderer techniques.

# Historical foundation retained from the prior project knowledge document

The material below is retained because it contains valuable earlier architecture, asset-cache experiments, and Test 18–20 history. It predates the direct-renderer V14–V17 architecture.

**When it conflicts with the current snapshot above, the current snapshot wins.**

---

# Build Royale Local-Only Customization — Functional Handoff

## 1. Current project direction

The project has been refactored to a **local-only client customization system**.

The end product should modify what the current browser displays without attempting to alter authoritative multiplayer cosmetic state.

The intended design is now:

```text
native Build Royale UI
        │
        ├─ custom controls injected into existing game controls
        │
        ├─ user chooses arbitrary bundled cosmetic/visual
        │
        ▼
local customization state
        │
        ▼
one-time/native-compatible asset substitution
        │
        ▼
normal game renderer
        │
        ▼
custom appearance visible locally
```

Further UI requirements will be supplied later.

The implementation should favor the game's existing renderer and asset system rather than maintaining a parallel rendering layer.

---

# 2. Working requirements

Use these constraints for future work.

* Changes only need to appear in the current browser.
* Do not design around remote-player visibility.
* Avoid continuous in-game hooks wherever possible.
* Avoid polling loops.
* Avoid `requestAnimationFrame` interception.
* Avoid persistent `drawImage` interception.
* Avoid persistent `MutationObserver` use unless genuinely necessary.
* Prefer initialization-time or one-shot substitutions.
* Remove temporary hooks immediately after the required asset has been captured/substituted.
* Reuse the game's native renderer.
* Reuse bundled game assets rather than reproducing them.
* Complete scripts are preferred over patches.
* Test scripts should be compact/minified.
* Diagnostic scripts should have `COPY LOG` when useful.
* Permanent controlled-test player name:

```text
unlocker_test_player
```

* Future work does not need to redact test-account token values if logging them is technically useful.
* Do not touch currency, Battle Pass, missions, XP, chests, purchasing, or similar systems.
* Do not redo already completed server-recognition research; local-only is now the final product.

---

# 3. Primary local cosmetic state

The game's normal locker state is stored at:

```javascript
localStorage.getItem("locker2")
```

Typical schema:

```json
{
  "wrap":"ice",
  "skin":"tennis",
  "pickaxe":"club",
  "trail":"trail1",
  "emotes":["emote0","emote1","emote2","emote3"],
  "glider":"glider"
}
```

A normal native-compatible locker commit is:

```javascript
function commitLocker(next){
  const current=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("locker2")||"{}");
  const merged={...current,...next};
  localStorage.setItem("locker2",JSON.stringify(merged));
  if(typeof window.Eâ$==="function")window.Eâ$();
  return merged;
}
```

This is useful for selections that should also behave normally in the native lobby UI.

For arbitrary local-only cosmetics, however, the selected visual does **not** have to equal the cosmetic stored in `locker2`.

That distinction should be embraced in the refactor.

Recommended conceptual state:

```text
nativeLocker
    = whatever Build Royale normally uses

localVisualOverrides
    = arbitrary bundled visuals selected by custom UI
```

Example:

```javascript
localVisualOverrides={
  skin:"baldeagle",
  pickaxe:"castleaxe"
};
```

The game's normal locker can remain:

```javascript
{
  skin:"tennis",
  pickaxe:"club",
  ...
}
```

while the renderer displays the override locally.

---

# 4. Known cosmetic asset paths

Useful direct asset patterns:

```text
Skin body:
  /cosmetics/body/<skin>.png

Skin head:
  /cosmetics/head/<skin>.png

Pickaxe:
  /cosmetics/pickaxe/<id>.png

Glider:
  /cosmetics/glider/<id>.png

Emote:
  /cosmetics/emotes/<id>.png

Wrap/combination:
  /cosmetics/combos/<id>.png

Trail-related:
  buildart/<trail>-0.png
  buildart/<trail>-1.png
```

Earlier asset enumeration found approximately:

```text
SKIN       178
GLIDER       7
WRAP        76
PICKAXE    162
TRAIL      154
EMOTES     208
```

Therefore the custom UI can be generated from the game's bundled catalog/assets rather than hardcoding only currently available locker items.

---

# 5. Important renderer behavior

## Skin

One `locker.skin` ID normally controls both:

```text
/cosmetics/body/<skin>.png
/cosmetics/head/<skin>.png
```

There is no separate normal cosmetic body/head protocol.

Therefore a full local skin override usually needs to substitute both body and head resources.

## Pickaxe

Normal match rendering requests:

```text
/cosmetics/pickaxe/<locker.pickaxe>.png
```

A local substitution can redirect that requested image to another bundled pickaxe.

## Glider

`locker.glider` is not the only relevant field.

Player state commonly contains:

```text
locker.glider = null
gliderSkin = "glider"
```

Future glider customization should therefore be approached from actual asset loading/rendering rather than simply changing `locker.glider`.

## `hair`

`hair` belongs to the game's default/built-in character appearance system.

It is not an independent cosmetic head slot.

## `layer`

`layer` is a rendering/world-layer field.

It should not be used as a cosmetic compositing control.

---

# 6. Critical asset-cache behavior

The game's internal asset loader caches resources by the **URL string**.

Therefore:

```text
cosmetics/body/tennis.png
```

and:

```text
cosmetics/body/tennis.png?2
```

are separate cache entries.

This explains several earlier results.

Observed native behavior:

```text
pregame preview body:
  cosmetics/body/<skin>.png?<cachebuster>

match body:
  cosmetics/body/<skin>.png
```

while the head commonly uses:

```text
pregame:
  cosmetics/head/<skin>.png

match:
  cosmetics/head/<skin>.png
```

with no query-string difference.

This is one of the most important findings for future implementation.

A preview cache modification may automatically survive into a match for the head but not the body.

---

# 7. Test 18 — preview-cache skin substitution

## Goal

Determine whether changing the already loaded native skin preview resources could affect match rendering.

Native skin:

```text
tennis
```

Local visual target:

```text
baldeagle
```

The test found:

```text
captured preview body:
  /cosmetics/body/tennis.png?2

captured preview head:
  /cosmetics/head/tennis.png
```

Both preview objects were changed to Bald Eagle resources.

## Result

Lobby preview:

```text
Bald Eagle body
Bald Eagle head
```

Match:

```text
Bald Eagle head
Tennis body
```

## Conclusion

The match reused the same no-query head asset object:

```text
/cosmetics/head/tennis.png
```

but did not reuse:

```text
/cosmetics/body/tennis.png?2
```

because the match independently requested:

```text
/cosmetics/body/tennis.png
```

This test revealed the exact cache-key distinction needed to solve full local skin substitution.

---

# 8. Test 19 — complete local skin substitution

## Goal

Display an arbitrary bundled skin completely in the match while leaving the normal locker unchanged.

Native locker skin:

```text
tennis
```

Local target:

```text
baldeagle
```

## Strategy

Two substitutions were used.

### Head

Capture/mutate the exact no-query native head cache entry:

```text
/cosmetics/head/tennis.png
```

so it loads:

```text
/cosmetics/head/baldeagle.png
```

### Body

Install a temporary `HTMLImageElement.src` setter interception for the exact upcoming match request:

```text
/cosmetics/body/tennis.png
```

and redirect that single request to:

```text
/cosmetics/body/baldeagle.png
```

After the match's body image had been created, restore the native setter immediately.

## Important log

```text
HEAD READY ... tennis head -> baldeagle
MATCH BODY INTERCEPT ... tennis body -> baldeagle
HTMLImageElement.src hook removed
```

## Result

Local match:

```text
Bald Eagle head
Bald Eagle body
```

The normal locker remained Tennis.

## Conclusion

**Full arbitrary bundled local skin substitution is proven.**

The correct implementation model is:

```text
normal locker ID
      │
      ├─ exact cached head asset replaced
      │
      └─ exact initial match body request redirected once
                │
                ▼
         remove interception
                │
                ▼
         native renderer continues normally
```

This is currently the best proven low-overhead skin technique.

---

# 9. Test 20 — local pickaxe substitution

## Goal

Test whether the same one-shot substitution concept works for pickaxes.

Native pickaxe:

```text
club
```

Selected arbitrary bundled target:

```text
castleaxe
```

Target metadata observed:

```text
Castle Axe
asset: 300x300
```

## Intercept

The match's normal request:

```text
/cosmetics/pickaxe/club.png
```

was redirected once to:

```text
/cosmetics/pickaxe/castleaxe.png
```

The temporary image-source hook was then removed.

## Result

The local player displayed:

```text
Castle Axe
```

during the match.

## Conclusion

**Arbitrary bundled local pickaxe substitution is proven.**

The same broad pattern should be assumed as the starting point for other image-based cosmetic categories:

```text
identify native requested resource
        ↓
redirect exact resource once
        ↓
allow game to cache/use object
        ↓
remove temporary hook
```

---

# 10. Generic one-shot image substitution pattern

This is the core pattern that should be generalized rather than installing long-running renderer hooks.

Conceptually:

```javascript
const d=Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(
  HTMLImageElement.prototype,
  "src"
);

const originalSet=d.set;

Object.defineProperty(
  HTMLImageElement.prototype,
  "src",
  {
    configurable:d.configurable,
    enumerable:d.enumerable,
    get:d.get,
    set(value){
      if(value===SOURCE){
        originalSet.call(this,TARGET);
        restore();
        return;
      }
      originalSet.call(this,value);
    }
  }
);
```

The actual implementation should account for absolute vs relative URL normalization.

The important lifecycle is:

```text
install
   ↓
wait for exact native resource request
   ↓
redirect one resource
   ↓
restore original descriptor
```

Do not leave the setter modified during normal gameplay if it is no longer needed.

---

# 11. Why one-shot substitution is preferred

Persistent interception was investigated but is undesirable for the final product.

Avoid designs such as:

```text
per-frame drawImage interception
persistent image-source interception
MutationObserver watching the entire game
polling for player state continuously
requestAnimationFrame wrapping
```

These can add unnecessary work during gameplay and make compatibility harder.

The proven one-shot approach moves essentially all customization overhead to initialization.

Once the game's normal render objects reference the desired image, normal rendering continues without the customization system needing to participate in every frame.

---

# 12. Recommended local skin implementation

A future generalized skin handler should approximately perform:

```text
1. Determine native skin ID.
2. Determine requested local visual skin ID.

3. Handle head:
   source:
     cosmetics/head/<native>.png

   desired:
     cosmetics/head/<override>.png

   modify/capture the resource used by the native cache.

4. Handle body:
   wait for:
     cosmetics/body/<native>.png

   redirect once to:
     cosmetics/body/<override>.png

5. Restore temporary image hook.

6. Let native renderer continue.
```

The custom UI should maintain the user's visual selection independently of `locker2`.

---

# 13. Recommended local pickaxe implementation

Approximately:

```text
native locker pickaxe:
  club

local visual pickaxe:
  castleaxe

wait for native:
  cosmetics/pickaxe/club.png

redirect once:
  cosmetics/pickaxe/castleaxe.png

restore hook
```

This behavior has already been demonstrated successfully.

---

# 14. Remaining cosmetic categories

The following categories were not individually pushed through the same complete proof sequence because the working image-substitution model had already been demonstrated sufficiently:

```text
wrap
trail
glider
emotes
```

Do not assume all four are implemented identically.

Instead, for each category:

```text
1. Locate actual render/resource dependency.
2. Identify the exact native asset URL/cache object.
3. Determine whether it is instantiated pregame or at first use.
4. Substitute at that point.
5. Remove temporary interception.
```

Useful likely paths:

```text
glider:
  /cosmetics/glider/<id>.png

wrap:
  /cosmetics/combos/<id>.png
  and/or underlying wrap resources

trail:
  buildart/<trail>-0.png
  buildart/<trail>-1.png

emote:
  /cosmetics/emotes/<id>.png
```

Gliders and trails may require state/use activation before their render assets are instantiated.

---

# 15. Native preview vs match rendering

The eventual UI may want changes visible immediately before a match.

There are therefore two distinct rendering targets:

```text
A. lobby/locker preview
B. live-match player
```

They may use different resource cache keys.

Do not treat successful lobby substitution as proof that match substitution is ready.

For skins specifically:

```text
head:
  preview and match can share cache

body:
  preview may use ?<cachebuster>
  match uses no-query resource
```

Future code should intentionally handle both contexts if an immediate preview is required.

---

# 16. Catalog/local-selection design

The final local customization UI should ideally use the full cosmetic catalog rather than `window.åÆÆ`.

Conceptually:

```text
full catalog
    │
    ├─ skin
    ├─ pickaxe
    ├─ wrap
    ├─ trail
    ├─ glider
    └─ emote
```

The visual selection state should belong to the customization layer itself.

Recommended conceptual structure:

```javascript
const LocalVisuals={
  skin:null,
  pickaxe:null,
  wrap:null,
  trail:null,
  glider:null,
  emotes:null
};
```

A value of `null` means:

```text
use the game's normal appearance
```

A non-null value means:

```text
replace the corresponding local visual with this bundled asset
```

This makes it easy to support per-category enable/disable behavior.

---

# 17. Suggested persistence

Do not overload `locker2` for local-only overrides.

Use a separate storage entry, for example:

```javascript
localStorage["br_local_visuals"]
```

Possible schema:

```json
{
  "enabled":true,
  "skin":"baldeagle",
  "pickaxe":"castleaxe",
  "wrap":null,
  "trail":null,
  "glider":null,
  "emotes":null
}
```

Benefits:

* native locker remains intact;
* disabling the customization restores normal appearance immediately;
* game updates are less likely to overwrite custom selections;
* native and custom choices can coexist;
* custom UI does not need to emulate ownership state.

---

# 18. Startup timing

The customization layer needs to initialize early enough to affect resources before the relevant match assets are created.

Likely lifecycle:

```text
page/game loaded
      ↓
custom UI/bootstrap installed
      ↓
read br_local_visuals
      ↓
prepare substitutions
      ↓
user presses Play
      ↓
game creates player render assets
      ↓
one-shot substitutions fire
      ↓
temporary hooks removed
```

A selector that is injected directly into existing game controls can update `br_local_visuals` at any time before Play.

---

# 19. Player targeting

For local-only modifications affecting only the current player, avoid replacing globally shared resources in ways that unintentionally change every player using the same native cosmetic.

Potential issue:

```text
local player native skin = tennis
remote player native skin = tennis
```

If the global cached `tennis` image object itself is permanently replaced with Bald Eagle, both players could potentially display Bald Eagle locally.

Therefore the final implementation must determine whether the relevant cached render object is:

```text
global/shared per asset
```

or:

```text
copied/assigned per player
```

before generalizing the existing test technique.

Earlier tests established that the local player's resources can be substituted successfully, but **per-player isolation should be explicitly verified during the refactor**.

This is one of the most important remaining implementation questions.

---

# 20. Existing player identification

Where player-specific targeting becomes necessary, the game player entity structure is:

```text
p:[entityId,"player",x,y,z,active]
```

The controlled current-player identity is:

```text
unlocker_test_player
```

A player object can therefore be recognized through:

```javascript
Array.isArray(o.p) &&
o.p[1]==="player" &&
o.name==="unlocker_test_player"
```

This should only be used if the final rendering integration actually needs player-specific state tracking.

Avoid continuous network-state monitoring if a one-time renderer-object association can be found instead.

---

# 21. Potential better integration point

The existing working implementation hooks browser image loading.

A cleaner final implementation may be possible by operating one level deeper at the game's own asset-loader/cache layer.

The relevant internal loader discovered during bundle analysis is:

```text
ÈÀE(...)
```

and the central asset registry is:

```text
Á
```

The ideal final architecture would be:

```text
custom selection
      ↓
game asset/cache object substitution
      ↓
native renderer
```

rather than:

```text
custom selection
      ↓
browser-wide HTMLImageElement interception
      ↓
game asset loader
      ↓
native renderer
```

Future static/runtime inspection should therefore prioritize finding a stable reference to:

```text
ÈÀE
Á
```

or the current-build equivalents.

If direct access is practical, it may eliminate the need for even temporary global image hooks.
````````

````````markdown
# 1. Core project rule

BRIO is a **local-only visual customization and practice/modifier layer**.

Cosmetic and modifier behavior only needs to change what the current user's browser renders.

Do not redesign around:

- arbitrary cosmetics becoming authoritative server state;
- changing server ownership;
- rewriting outbound start packets;
- WebSocket manipulation;
- MessagePack ownership/cosmetic spoofing;
- causing other clients to see BRIO-selected cosmetics.

The game's native authoritative state should remain native unless the user explicitly changes that requirement later.

---

# 2. Performance rule

Performance is a hard requirement.

The production design should avoid:

```text
per-frame global Canvas interception
requestAnimationFrame wrapping
persistent broad Array.prototype.push hooks
persistent broad HTMLImageElement.src interception
global MutationObservers over the game
high-frequency whole-world polling

```

Recon-only temporary hooks are acceptable if:

- narrowly scoped;
- self-restoring;
- clearly labeled recon-only;
- not silently retained as the production architecture.

Preferred production pattern:

1. capture a native renderer/object once;
2. alter native renderer/resource state;
3. let the game's renderer continue normally.

---

# 3. Stable cosmetic architecture

The stable cosmetic design captures the local player's native renderer immediately after Play with a brief `Array.prototype.push` / `unshift` observation.

The global hook is restored as soon as capture goals are met.

Cosmetics are then applied directly to native renderer fields/resources.

Preserve per-player isolation.

The client can remove remote renderers from the active array at distance.

then freeze

For player indicators, false precision is worse than disappearing.

V35 implemented:

Runtime verification later reported approximately:

```text

errors: 0

```

Despite that:

**USER VISUAL RESULT: FAILED**

The marker disappeared from:

```text
the minimap
the full-size map

exactly as it normally does.

This is a critical architectural result.

It disproves the hypothesis:

```text
continually repainting the captured 1800x1800 canvas is sufficient

```

Do not repeat the same strategy.

Likely explanations to investigate:

- the map canvas is cleared/rebuilt after BRIO paints;
- the captured canvas is only an intermediate/stale buffer;
- another source canvas/state object is regenerated later;
- minimap/full map read from a different canonical map state;
- the game reconstructs the full map each draw from marker data and overwrites BRIO's direct canvas edits.

Next meteor recon should locate and modify the native marker/state object or the map render source that causes `ping-meteor-icon.png` to be drawn.

Preferred next direction:

```text
trace upward from the meteor draw to the object/function/state that decides whether the marker exists

```

not another generic per-frame Canvas repaint.

Static bundle analysis is likely useful here.
````````
